script:
Hello, this is The Portfolio Podcast for MEME. Thursday — here is your MEME recap. The portfolio closed up nineteen point four six percent on the session. That is a historic single-day move, and nearly every position in the book contributed.

TeraWulf just signed a twenty-year power contract with Anthropic worth nineteen billion dollars. That number is not a typo. It is one of the largest AI infrastructure commitments ever made to a single operator, and the stock moved accordingly.

No broad macro data was available for Thursday's session. Markets appeared to rally broadly on AI infrastructure momentum, with technology and industrial names leading the advance. The session's gains were driven largely by company-specific catalysts rather than index-level macro prints, suggesting the move was idiosyncratic rather than a rising-tide effect across the full market.

Bloom Energy is the top story of Thursday's session, and it earns that designation on two separate legs. First, the company's second-quarter results finally cleared the market, delivering numbers strong enough to pull the entire fuel-cell sector higher. Mizuho followed with a formal upgrade, moving Bloom Energy to outperform from neutral and attaching a price target implying forty-eight percent upside from Wednesday's closing price. That target is two hundred forty-two dollars. The thesis centers on AI-driven electricity demand from data centers, which is creating structural, long-duration load growth that energy hardware providers are uniquely positioned to capture. Bloom Energy surged twenty-six point four nine percent on the session. The Mizuho call and earnings combination gave institutional buyers a clear entry framework, and the volume confirmed it.

Applied Optoelectronics was up seventeen point seven six percent on the session. No company-specific news drove the move, but the name trades directly in the optical networking supply chain feeding AI data center buildout — the same infrastructure theme dominating Thursday's tape. Watch for any commentary from hyperscale customers on interconnect demand.

Redwire Corporation gained eight point eight seven percent on the session. The company announced it will report second-quarter twenty twenty-six financial results after market close on Wednesday, August fifth. That date is now the nearest hard catalyst for the position. Execution against guidance will be the key test.

AST SpaceMobile rose ten point two zero percent on the session. A published comparison piece weighed AST SpaceMobile against Lockheed Martin on growth and valuation — the framing alone signals that analysts are taking the company's scale ambitions seriously. Cash burn relative to satellite deployment progress remains the metric to monitor.

Turning to Nebius Group. The stock gained twenty-seven point one three percent on Thursday's session, the second-largest single-day move in the primary holdings. The driver was a fresh AI partnership announcement that reignited the infrastructure trade across cloud names. A finance publication noted the company still screens as undervalued on market multiples despite a one-hundred-seventy-two point three percent return over the past twelve months. The Nvidia stake and long-term cloud positioning remain the structural anchors. How much of the AI reset is already priced in is the live debate.

Over at Bloom Energy — already covered as the top story — twenty-six point four nine percent on the session. August fifth earnings at Redwire will also test whether the industrial AI infrastructure narrative has legs beyond the software layer.

TeraWulf jumped eighteen point zero nine percent on the session. The nineteen-billion-dollar Anthropic deal is a twenty-year power commitment — that duration is the critical detail. It converts a speculative mining operator into something closer to a contracted infrastructure utility. One analyst piece flagged that TeraWulf and a peer are up more than fifty percent in twenty twenty-six while IREN has lagged, raising a potential catch-up trade thesis.

Lumentum Holdings rose fifteen point zero nine percent on the session. No direct company news, but Lumentum sits in the same optical components space as Applied Optoelectronics, and the sector moved in unison Thursday. Earnings season will be the next clarifying event.

IREN Limited surged thirty point five four percent on the session — the largest single-day gain in the primary holdings Thursday. The same analyst note comparing TeraWulf and IREN pointed out that IREN carries the largest GPU partnership and power portfolio among its peer group, yet has lagged in year-to-date performance. Thursday's move may represent that reversion beginning to close.

Sandisk Corporation closed up twenty-five point nine nine percent on the session. No company-specific news was available. Storage hardware names have benefited from the broader AI infrastructure bid, as data density requirements for model training and inference continue to expand. Quarterly results will be the next fundamental checkpoint.

Three data points to watch in the next forty-eight hours. First, Redwire Corporation reports second-quarter twenty twenty-six results after market close on Wednesday, August fifth — the nearest hard earnings date for this portfolio. Second, any follow-through analyst commentary on the Mizuho Bloom Energy upgrade and whether additional desks move to match the outperform call. Third, watch for Anthropic or TeraWulf to provide additional deal structure details on the nineteen-billion-dollar contract — duration terms and payment mechanics will matter to how the market values that revenue stream.

This is The Portfolio Podcast for MEME. We will be back same time the next business day with tomorrow's news. Watch whether Thursday's AI infrastructure momentum carries into Friday's open, or whether the session's outsized gains invite profit-taking across the board.
